options.region: Home region must be Singapore (ap-singapore-1 or another eligible Singapore home region)
options.cpu: 2 Arm OCPUs total under the current Always Free allowance
options.storage: Up to 200 GB combined boot and block volume storage in the home region; the default boot volume is 50 GB
options.bandwidth: 10 TB outbound data per month under current Always Free resources
options.private_access: Supported through SSH plus Tailscale or WireGuard; public IPv4 assignment is optional and OCI networking can place an instance in a private subnet.
billing_caveats: Always Free compute and volume resources must be created in the tenancy home region.
Usage above the Always Free limits, non-home-region volumes, or paid add-ons can incur charges.
Free A1 capacity may be unavailable and Oracle explicitly documents out-of-host-capacity errors.
Idle Always Free instances may be reclaimed when CPU, network, and memory remain below documented thresholds for seven days.
options.compatibility_note: This is Arm-only for the useful free shape. The repository, native C++ build, Node dependencies, and Docker images have not been proven as a complete arm64 deployment contract; x86-only binaries or images could fail.
options.availability_note: Free-tier capacity is explicitly not guaranteed, and an idle polling host can be reclaimed. It is appropriate only as an experiment after an arm64 clean-build proof, not as the first dependable central host.
options.fit: Zero-cost experiment that meets memory and storage needs, but it has the highest architecture, capacity, and lifecycle risk.

recommendation.reason: It is the least expensive currently verified paid Singapore x86_64 option in this shortlist and exactly matches the preferred 4-vCPU, 8-GB, 160-GB shape. It provides a normal unmanaged Linux VM, so deployment is performed over SSH and does not depend on the GitHub deployment systems that have been failing.
recommendation.fallback_reason: It offers the same shape and Singapore location for USD 48 per month with simple per-second billing and a mature Droplet workflow.
recommendation.large_provider_fallback_reason: It is USD 44 per month and meets the minimum, but has only two vCPUs and therefore less build/backfill headroom.
recommendation.ultra_budget_latency_tradeoff: Hetzner EU CX33 at USD 9.99 per month excluding IPv4 and tax meets the minimum 4-vCPU, 8-GB, 80-GB shape, but should be selected only if Singapore latency is not important.
recommendation.do_not_select_first_reason: The repository has no current full arm64 deployment proof, while OCI documents both free-capacity failures and idle-instance reclamation.
recommendation.provisioning_boundary: Before spending money, confirm the provider account can create the exact plan in the target region. Then provision one Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 VM, restrict ingress to SSH or the overlay VPN, install Docker Engine and Compose v2, clone the repository, create .env.central locally with mode 0600, run the repository central-host preflight, and only then start web plus the single backfill writer.

tradeoffs.benefit: Lowest latency from Vietnam, low compatibility risk, predictable capacity, and direct reuse of the tested Docker/Compose deployment path.
tradeoffs.cost: Approximately USD 40-58 per month before taxes and optional backups.

tradeoffs.benefit: Approximately USD 9.99 per month before IPv4 and tax with 4 vCPUs, 8 GB RAM, 80 GB NVMe, and generous EU traffic.
tradeoffs.cost: Higher Vietnam-to-Europe latency and a region farther from the operator; this is acceptable for unattended polling but less pleasant for interactive dashboard use.

tradeoffs.benefit: No monthly compute cost with 12 GB RAM and up to 200 GB total boot/block storage.
tradeoffs.cost: Unproven arm64 repo compatibility, no guaranteed capacity, and possible idle-resource reclamation.

tradeoffs.benefit: No new VM subscription and native x86_64 compatibility.
tradeoffs.cost: Depends on stable power, connectivity, remote recovery, Docker/Compose availability, and the operator accepting that the workstation becomes the always-on production-like host.

unknowns: The maximum monthly budget and whether USD 40-48 per month is acceptable were not specified.
Provider account eligibility, payment-method acceptance, identity verification, and regional quota have not been tested; these can block provisioning even when a plan is advertised.
No latency measurements from the operator's Vietnam network to Singapore, Jakarta, or European regions were collected.
The current cache growth rate and required retention period were not measured, so 80-160 GB is a starting capacity rather than a long-term guarantee.
Optional backup requirements and acceptable recovery-point/recovery-time objectives were not specified.
No provider was purchased, provisioned, or contacted during this research task.
No arm64 clean build, full suite, or Docker deployment was run, so Oracle A1 remains compatibility-unproven.
